cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Kernels – small, soft, or edible parts of a nut, seed, or corn; metaphorically, tiny bits.

p.em: Example: He only threw her a few kernels of affection, keeping her wanting more.

cosy-blockquote.p: Delusional – characterized by or holding idiosyncratic beliefs or impressions that are contradicted by reality.

p.em: Example: He was delusional to think he could win without practicing at all.

cosy-blockquote.p: Obsession – an unhealthy preoccupation with someone or something.

p.em: Example: His obsession with cleanliness became a bit extreme.

cosy-blockquote.p: cactus – A succulent plant with thick fleshy stems and spines, adapted to arid conditions.

p.em: Example: Living in a harsh emotional desert requires resilience, much like a thriving cactus.

cosy-blockquote.p: drought – A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall, leading to a shortage of water.

p.em: Example: An emotional drought can leave you feeling drained until genuine connection returns.

cosy-blockquote.p: symbolism – the use of symbols to represent ideas or qualities.

p.em: Example: The director used rich visual symbolism to convey the deeper theme.

cosy-blockquote.p: stockpile – A large accumulated stock or reserve of goods or materials kept for future use.

p.em: Example: She built a stockpile of emergency supplies and bottled water just in case of unexpected trouble.

cosy-blockquote.p: compliment – a polite expression of praise or admiration.

p.em: Example: He felt wonderful after receiving a sincere compliment from his teacher.

cosy-blockquote.p: scarcity – The state of being scarce or in short supply; shortage.

p.em: Example: Living with a mindset of emotional scarcity makes people cling desperately to crumbs.

cosy-blockquote.p: patience – the capacity to accept or tolerate delay or trouble.

p.em: Example: Learning to play an instrument requires a lot of patience.

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
